title: the delete gate reads .cairn as the guarded root only where it is a path segment
intention: The delete gate refuses every delete under ~/.cairn and stops refusing text that only contains '.cairn' inside another word or a regex, so the guard is never routed around for harmless work.
why: Law 4 and Law 7: a physics gate that misfires teaches the reflex of scripting around it. bin/cmd/deletegate refused 4 commands that delete nothing under ~/.cairn, each worked around by moving the text into a scratch file (n=2 on 2026-11-05, recorded in /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/ideas/2026-11-05-bin-cmd-deletegate-refused-two-commands-on.json; n=2 on 2026-11-20 by akiendelllinux_cc_0). 2026-11-20 #1: a python heredoc patching isolation.py whose new code made a probe dir with prefix ".cairn-swap-probe-" under /var/tmp and removed it with os.rmdir. 2026-11-20 #2: a read-only grep of bin/cmd/deletegate for the pattern "rmdir\|rmtree\|unlink\|...\|\.cairn". 2026-11-05: a heredoc patching server.py (sock.unlink) and a grep for "unlink|.cairn". In every case the guarded form that matched is GUARDED_FORMS' bare ".cairn" (deletegate:84), read as a substring: inside a longer word (.cairn-swap-probe-) or inside a regex (\.cairn\|). None of the four names a path at or under ~/.cairn..
how: In bin/cmd/deletegate, replace the substring test `any(form in command for form in GUARDED_FORMS)` with one regex: `.cairn` counts as the guarded root only where it is a whole path segment, preceded by start, whitespace, '/', '~', a quote, '=', '(' or a backtick and followed by end, '/', whitespace, a quote, ';', '&', '|', ')' or a backtick. Every GUARDED_FORMS spelling (~/.cairn, $HOME/.cairn, <home>/.cairn) ends in '/.cairn' so it is covered by the same regex. Co-occurrence is kept exactly: the verb and the root are still asked of the whole text independently. Proof: add teeth to bin/proofs/test_delete_gate.py under a PROVES key for this ticket, one per clause; clause 3 names the existing co-occurrence tooth.

clauses.claim: each of the four measured commands, reduced to its matching text (a heredoc whose code calls os.rmdir on a /var/tmp dir with prefix '.cairn-swap-probe-'; grep -n "rmdir\|\.cairn" bin/cmd/deletegate; a heredoc calling sock.unlink(); grep "unlink|.cairn" bin/cmd/deletegate), passes the gate

every guarded delete still refuses: each spelling in test_every_spelling_of_the_same_delete_is_caught, the quoted and python-call teeth, and the bare relative root (cd ~ && rm -rf .cairn/logs; rm -rf .cairn; rmdir ".cairn/x"; shutil.rmtree('.cairn'))
the co-occurrence over-refusals stay refused (test_the_match_is_by_CO_OCCURRENCE_..., unchanged): the narrowing reads the root's spelling as a path, it does not parse clauses

decisions.text: D1: GUARDED_FORMS' substring test becomes one path-segment regex for .cairn; co-occurrence unchanged.
D2: teeth in the existing proof, one per clause, under this ticket's PROVES key.
